question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) system?

options.D: Storing digital patient medical data securely

explanation: Think of an EHR as a secure digital folder for everything about a patient. It is built to store, update, and safely share their health info across the hospital! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do EHRs help nurses and doctors work better across different hospital wards?

options.A: By removing the need for physical checks
options.D: By allowing real-time sharing of patient notes

explanation: You've got this! When everyone can see up-to-date notes instantly on the system, patient care becomes smoother no matter who is on duty. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: What was a major safety headache with old-school paper medical records?
explanation: Ah, bad handwriting! Messy doctor or nurse notes on paper charts often led to drug mix-ups and confusion. Digital systems totally solve this. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why did hospitals start moving away from paper files to digital health systems?

options.A: To make patient records public to anyone
options.B: To improve data retrieval speed and storage efficiency
options.C: To stop nurses from writing care notes
options.D: To increase the physical space needed for archives

explanation: Digital files mean no more digging through dusty rooms for old folders. Everything pops up on screen in seconds! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which part of an EHR system helps warn clinicians if a patient is allergic to a prescribed drug?
explanation: Clinical decision support tools act like a smart assistant, popping up safety alerts when they spot potential drug allergies or bad drug mixes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of typing medication orders into a computer instead of writing them on paper?

options.A: Replacing the need for bedside nurses
options.B: Making doctors spend more time typing
options.D: Reducing errors caused by poor handwriting

explanation: Typed orders are clear and straightforward, cutting out guesswork and keeping patients safe from handwriting mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a key feature of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR)?

options.A: It is run only by government agencies
options.B: It shares data easily across multiple hospital networks
options.D: It is usually limited to a single clinic or facility

explanation: Remember, an EMR is like a digital chart for just one specific clinic, whereas an EHR is much broader! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is an EHR considered a step up and more comprehensive than an EMR?

options.A: It only contains billing and insurance info
options.B: It brings together patient data from multiple healthcare organizations
options.C: It removes the need for physical patient exams
options.D: It is only used by doctors

explanation: EHRs connect the dots! They let different hospitals and clinics share and view the same patient history. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: How do EHR systems directly improve medication safety for hospitalized patients?

options.A: By making medication administration completely optional
options.B: By allowing patients to purchase medications online directly
options.C: By removing the pharmacist from the medication delivery chain
options.D: By utilizing barcode scanning to verify patient identity and drugs

explanation: Barcode medication administration checks ensure the right drug is given to the correct patient at the right time. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: A ward nurse notices a patient's vital signs worsening on the electronic chart. What makes the EHR so helpful here?

options.A: Spotting early signs of clinical deterioration quickly
options.B: Locking out other nurses from the chart
options.D: Printing a paper bill for accounts

explanation: Digital charts show clear trends over time, helping you catch warning signs early and save lives before things get critical. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is a major challenge when trying to use EHRs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Unstable electricity supply and frequent power outages

explanation: Power supply hiccups can make running computers and servers quite tough, which is a big hurdle for tech adoption. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why might some experienced healthcare staff be hesitant to switch to electronic records?

options.A: No patients want to visit digital hospitals
options.B: The belief that computers cause illness
options.C: Comfort and familiarity with traditional paper documentation
options.D: Rules forbid nurses from touching computers

explanation: Change is hard! Many staff members are simply so used to paper charts that learning a new digital system feels intimidating at first. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is a golden rule for keeping patient data safe when using an EHR workstation?

options.A: Logging out or locking the screen before walking away
options.B: Writing your password on a sticky note on the monitor
options.C: Sharing your login with nursing students on duty
options.D: Leaving records open on display for visitors to read

explanation: Always lock your screen when you step away! It keeps patient privacy secure from unauthorized eyes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)

question: How do role-based access controls protect electronic health records?

options.A: By making all patient records public
options.B: By requiring patients to approve every nurse login
options.C: By restricting staff viewing permissions to their specific job scope
options.D: By deleting patient files after every shift change

explanation: Role-based access means you only see the info you need for your specific duties, keeping patient data private and secure. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is an exciting feature expected in future nursing EHR systems?

options.A: Predictive analytics to warn against impending complications

explanation: Future tech will use data trends to spot trouble before it happens, helping nurses stay one step ahead in patient care! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h8)

question: How do wearable health monitors connect with modern electronic health records?

options.A: By syncing patient vital signs directly into digital charts
options.C: By printing paper reports for the supervisor
options.D: By sending text messages to hospital security

explanation: Wearable gadgets can feed live health data straight into the EHR, saving you from writing down every single number manually. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h8)
